sense: of a person: doing well in life, prosperous

terms.grammar: adjective, third declension, one ending (participle of flōreō)
evidence: Caes. BG 7.32: flōrentem et illūstrem adulēscentem
Cic. Fam. 2.13.2: hominem flōrentem aetāte, opibus, honōribus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of persons and states in their prime, rich in means, office or fame; the verb is flōrēre, to flourish.

evidence: Cic. Rep. 2.9: bella cum fīnitimīs fēlīcissimē multa gessit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Par. 18: quī tē beātum, quī flōrentem putās

phrases.latin: tē miseriae, tē aerumnae premunt omnēs, quī tē beātum, quī flōrentem putās
phrases.english: every misery and every trouble weighs on you, who think yourself happy and successful

sources: Lewis & Short: floreo · Lewis & Short: felix · Lewis & Short: beatus
Caesar (BG 7.32) and Cicero (Par. 18) checked against the Perseus Latin texts.
